subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual group activation for unmentioned Telegram and WhatsApp group messages, and if so should it be a shared channel/plugin SDK contract or channel-specific core behavior?
rationale: The request changes when shared-room content reaches model providers, adds public config and fallback-model behavior, and crosses Telegram, WhatsApp, plugin, session-state, logging, and security boundaries; automation cannot safely choose that product/security contract.

options.title: Design shared activation contract
options.body: Create a default-off cross-channel contract for contextual activation with explicit privacy, provider, logging, and state semantics before implementing channel integrations.

options.title: Defer to narrower tracks
options.body: Keep this as an umbrella and pursue attention-window, per-mention routing, or passive hook work only through the existing narrower issues and PRs.

options.title: Reject ambient LLM peeking
options.body: Keep requireMention, always-on ambient rooms, and passive history as the supported safety model and document model-driven peeking as out of scope for core.

recommendation.title: Design shared activation contract
recommendation.body: Create a default-off cross-channel contract for contextual activation with explicit privacy, provider, logging, and state semantics before implementing channel integrations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal across shared mention policy, group activation parsing, group docs, ambient-room behavior, and prior review comments on this exact boundary.
